original_question: Which genetic disorder of the connective tissue, caused by a mutation in the FBN1 gene, is associated with an acute cardiovascular condition that presents with a sudden onset of agonizing chest or back pain?

final_qi.question: Which genetic disorder of the connective tissue, caused by a mutation in the FBN1 gene, is associated with an acute cardiovascular condition that presents with a sudden onset of agonizing chest or back pain?
final_qi.long_answer: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal-dominant connective-tissue disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the FBN1 gene encoding fibrillin-1. Patients with Marfan syndrome have weakness of the aortic media that predisposes them to acute aortic dissection, a cardiovascular emergency that classically presents with sudden, tearing chest or back pain.

final_answer.long_answer: Marfan syndrome is an inherited connective-tissue disorder produced by pathogenic variants in the FBN1 gene, which encodes fibrillin-1. Patients with Marfan syndrome have weakened elastic fibers in the aortic media, predisposing them to acute aortic dissection—a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency that classically presents with the sudden onset of tearing or agonizing chest or back pain.
